title: Company sync accelerator - compact brief
content:
Purpose:
A compact playbook for running a focused company-wide sync week ("accelerator") to align product, engineering, SRE, and GTM on a single adapt cycle. This is intentionally short — use as the working checklist for the week and the seed for the all-hands segment.

Context and why now:
- Observed friction: multiple teams making local tradeoffs on model variants, batching defaults, and rollout policies that increased tail latency incidents in Jan–Feb 2026.
- Business need: shift to a reliability + unit-economics sprint ahead of capacity commits for Dedicated and Private this quarter.
- Timebox: run a 5-day focused sync with light pre-reads and a short public all-hands update at the end.

Week objective (single sentence):
- Reach cross-functional agreement on the top 3 company levers for the next quarter (latency SLO, cost-per-token target, rollout/fallback policy) and lock owners + immediate next steps to hit those levers.

Three candidate company levers (proposed):
1) Latency SLO convergence: 95th-percentile tail <= 180ms for hosted-api default family for short-chat workloads.
   - Why: customer support and benchmark noise indicate variability is the primary product risk.
   - Draft metric: p95 response time (50–512 token requests) measured per-route.
2) Unit cost target: 20% reduction in tokens-per-dollar for high-throughput embeddings and reranking flows via batching and caching.
   - Why: Dedicated procurement conversations hinge on predictable unit economics.
   - Draft metric: tokens/US$ over a 30-day rolling window for defined workload buckets.
3) Rollout & fallback baseline: ship a standardized canary + auto-fallback policy for model variants across hosted and dedicated within 8 weeks.
   - Why: graceful degradation is core to reliability and enterprise SLAs.
   - Draft metric: percent of routes with enforced rollout policy and measured fallback success rate.

Draft OKR set (compact) — for discussion:
- Objective (Q2-ish): Harden serving economics and tail reliability so customers experience predictable throughput and lower unit costs.
  - KR1: Reduce p95 latency for default short-chat route from current baseline to <= 180ms (measurement: per-route p95).
  - KR2: Achieve 20% net improvement in tokens-per-$ for the top 5 production workloads (identified by traffic).
  - KR3: Implement rollout+fallback policy in 80% of customer-facing routes and validate in staged traffic.
  - KR4: Produce a runbook and SLIs for Dedicated capacity bursts with runbook verified in two scheduled exercises.

Owner suggestions (initial):
- Latency SLO convergence: Riley Chen (serving-runtime) + Maya Singh (SRE)
- Unit cost workstream: Diego Morales (Optimize) + Product-hosted-api
- Rollout & fallback: Tomiko Watanabe (Console + Rollouts) + Solutions Eng for canary design
- Runbook & exercises: eng-sre lead + customer-success for validation schedule

Week structure (recommended):
- Day -3 (pre-read sent): short baseline metrics, known blockers, and proposed levers (this doc as the one-pager).
- Day 0 (kickoff): 90-minute cross-functional kickoff, share baseline dashboards, align on levers and owners.
- Day 1–3 (deep work): parallel breakouts per lever (Latency, Cost, Rollouts) with synthesized quick experiments / small deploys. Each breakout produces: 1) clear next-steps, 2) a short experiment to run, 3) owners and required infra.
- Day 4 (integration): sync to reconcile cross-dependencies, finalize draft OKRs and decision log.
- End-of-week: 30-minute company all-hands slot (20 min update, 10 min Q&A) and public post summarizing decisions + action tracker.

All-hands content outline (30 minutes):
- 2 min intro (CEO/Head of Ops) — why accelerator and expected outcome
- 8 min baseline & signals (SRE/Product) — p95, cost trends, support tickets impact
- 10 min commitments (leads) — announce agreed levers, owners, and KRs with timelines
- 6 min what to expect (eng/product/CS) — planned rollouts, customer comms, and how teams should adjust
- 4 min live Q&A (or use slido + collected questions to keep time)

Communications cadence and ownership:
- Pre-read + survey (ops) — Day -3 — owner: Asha Patel
- Internal decision log (doc) — updated during week — owner: Diego Morales
- Public all-hands update + blog-lite post — Day 5 — owner: Head of Comms + Product
- Customer-facing comms (enterprise customers) — post-accelerator outreach — owner: Customer-success manager

Decision log (format notes) — keep as single-page list with: decision, rationale, owner, date, blockers, next step. Example entries to seed: 
- Decision: Aim for p95 <= 180ms for short-chat default. Rationale: reduce support noise, competitive benchmark. Owner: Riley Chen. Date: 2026-03-01. Next step: identify 3 candidate kernel/time-slicing improvements to test.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Localized optimizations cause model-quality regressions. Mitigation: pair cost/latency experiments with a small eval set and revert policy.
- Risk: Siloed rollouts across Dedicated vs Hosted lead to inconsistent customer experience. Mitigation: create a shared rollout policy library and require canaries for both surfaces.
- Risk: Overcommit to ambitious KR that needs infra changes. Mitigation: commit to a staging exercise before locking KR.

Quick checklist for leads (working doc mode):
- [ ] Confirm metrics owners and dashboards (Day 0)
- [ ] Small deploy plan for latency experiment (Day 1)
- [ ] Batching/caching quick wins list (Day 2)
- [ ] Draft rollout policy and canary config (Day 2–3)
- [ ] Coordinate customer outreach language (Day 4)
- [ ] Publish all-hands post and decision log (Day 5)

Notes to self / open questions to capture in pre-read survey:
- Which three production routes should be prioritized for p95 measurement? (ops/product input required)
- Are there existing Dedicated customers willing to participate in a controlled fallback test? (CS to coordinate)
- What is the smallest safe experiment to validate quantization/batching gains without regression? (APPLIED-ML input)

Appendix (links and quick references):
- Short metrics dashboard (link placeholder)
- Recent incident timeline (Feb 2026) (link placeholder)
- Template: decision log (link placeholder)

End — use this as the canonical compact playbook. Update iteratively during the accelerator and move final decisions into the org decision register. 

-- Asha
